bong-cai-xao-toi.name: Garlic Stir-Fried Broccoli
bong-cai-xao-toi.serving_basis: Two portions of stir-fried broccoli served with rice in a family vegetarian meal.
bong-cai-xao-toi.description: Green broccoli is briefly blanched, then tossed with fragrant garlic to retain its fresh color and gentle crunch—a simple vegetable dish for a weekday vegetarian meal.
bong-cai-xao-toi.finished_dish: Tender-crisp broccoli florets are lightly coated with garlic oil, with little moisture on the plate.
bong-cai-xao-toi.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, braised tofu or a light vegetable soup.
tips: Cut the florets into similar sizes so they cook evenly.
Blanch briefly and drain well before stir-frying.
Use high heat for a short time to keep the broccoli from turning soft.
bong-cai-xao-toi.image_alt: Garlic stir-fried broccoli on a pale ceramic plate, with bright green florets and golden garlic slices.
bong-cai-xao-toi.time_note: About 25 minutes including prep and cooking; the broccoli is briefly blanched first to preserve color and crunch.
suggested_pairings: Vegetarian braised tofu with straw mushrooms

ingredients.name: Green broccoli
ingredients.notes: Separate into bite-sized florets and rinse.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel, lightly crush and roughly mince.

preparation_steps.instruction: Separate the broccoli into small florets, rinse and drain. Peel and roughly mince the garlic.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the broccoli briefly, just until bright green; drain well.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a pan and saute the garlic until fragrant and just golden.
Add the broccoli and toss quickly over high heat. Season with salt and vegetarian seasoning, stir-fry until just tender, then turn off the heat.

bong-cai-xao-toi.media_alt_text: Green broccoli stir-fried with garlic on a light ceramic plate, with glossy florets and golden garlic slices.

cai-ngong-xao-toi.name: Garlic Stir-Fried Flowering Mustard Greens
cai-ngong-xao-toi.serving_basis: Two portions of garlic stir-fried Chinese flowering cabbage served with rice in a vegetarian family meal.
cai-ngong-xao-toi.description: Crisp flowering mustard greens are quickly cooked with fragrant garlic and a splash of water—a familiar green side dish for everyday meals.
cai-ngong-xao-toi.finished_dish: The stems retain a light crunch while the leaves soften, with a clean garlic aroma and little liquid on the plate.
cai-ngong-xao-toi.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a tofu dish or light soup.
tips: Choose greens with tender stems and fresh leaves; remove fibrous ends.
Add water gradually so the greens cook without needing a long covered simmer.
Season near the end and stop once the stems are just tender.
cai-ngong-xao-toi.image_alt: Garlic stir-fried flowering mustard greens on a pale celadon plate, with glossy green stems and golden garlic.
cai-ngong-xao-toi.time_note: About 15 minutes from prep to serving; stir-fry briefly so the greens stay crisp.
suggested_pairings: Yardlong beans stir-fried with straw mushrooms

ingredients.name: Flowering mustard greens
ingredients.notes: Remove tough stems, cut into bite-sized lengths and rinse.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add a little at a time during stir-frying.

preparation_steps.instruction: Remove damaged or tough sections of the greens, cut into bite-sized lengths, rinse and drain.
Peel and crush the garlic so it releases its aroma when sauteed.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil over medium heat and saute the garlic until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add the greens and toss for about 30 seconds. Add water gradually and stir-fry for 3–5 minutes.
Season with vegetarian granules and salt to taste. Turn off the heat as soon as the stems are tender.

cai-ngong-xao-toi.media_alt_text: Tender-crisp Chinese broccoli stir-fried with garlic on a pale green ceramic plate.

canh-sup-lo-thap-cam-chay.name: Vegetarian Mixed Broccoli Soup
canh-sup-lo-thap-cam-chay.serving_basis: Four bowls of mixed vegetable soup for a family meal.
canh-sup-lo-thap-cam-chay.description: Broccoli, cabbage, pumpkin and carrot simmer together for a naturally sweet vegetable soup; broccoli goes in near the end so it does not overcook.
canh-sup-lo-thap-cam-chay.finished_dish: Clear broth with tender vegetables that keep their shape; pumpkin is soft and the broccoli and carrot retain their color.
canh-sup-lo-thap-cam-chay.serving: Serve hot as the soup course with rice and a tofu or mushroom dish.
tips: Cut the vegetables into similar sizes so they cook evenly.
Simmer the pumpkin and carrot first; add broccoli near the end.
Season lightly after the vegetables have released their flavor.
canh-sup-lo-thap-cam-chay.image_alt: A bowl of vegetarian mixed broccoli soup with broccoli, cabbage, pumpkin and carrot in clear broth.
canh-sup-lo-thap-cam-chay.time_note: About 35 minutes including prep and cooking; add broccoli at the end to retain a slight bite.
suggested_pairings: Vegetarian braised tofu with straw mushrooms

ingredients.name: Cabbage
ingredients.notes: Separate the leaves, rinse and cut into pieces.

ingredients.name: Pumpkin
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into medium chunks.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use for the soup; adjust to the pot size.

preparation_steps.instruction: Separate the broccoli into florets and rinse. Wash the cabbage, pumpkin, carrot and onion, then cut them into bite-sized pieces.

cooking_steps.instruction: Add the onion, carrot, cabbage and pumpkin to a pot with water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 15 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the broccoli and simmer for another 3–5 minutes, until it reaches the desired tenderness.
Season lightly with salt, taste the broth and turn off the heat.

canh-sup-lo-thap-cam-chay.media_alt_text: A bowl of mixed vegetable soup with broccoli, cabbage, pumpkin and carrot in a clear broth.

dau-dua-xao-nam-rom-chay.name: Vegetarian Yardlong Beans with Straw Mushrooms
dau-dua-xao-nam-rom-chay.serving_basis: Four portions of yardlong beans and straw mushrooms served with rice in a vegetarian meal.
dau-dua-xao-nam-rom-chay.description: Green yardlong beans are quickly tossed with tender straw mushrooms and plant-based seasoning—a low-fuss stir-fry that adds vegetables and mushrooms to a weekday meal.
dau-dua-xao-nam-rom-chay.finished_dish: The beans remain tender-crisp and lightly seasoned, paired with soft, savory straw mushrooms and a touch of pepper.
dau-dua-xao-nam-rom-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice; add a vegetable soup for a more complete vegetarian meal.
tips: Cut the beans into even lengths so they cook at the same pace.
Rinse the mushrooms gently and drain them well before cooking.
Use high heat and keep the beans moving so they do not release excess water.
search_terms: vegetarian yardlong beans with straw mushrooms
dau-dua-xao-nam-rom-chay.image_alt: Vegetarian yardlong beans and straw mushrooms on a rustic ceramic plate, lightly browned and just cooked.
dau-dua-xao-nam-rom-chay.time_note: About 25 minutes including prep and stir-frying; cook the mushrooms briefly before adding the beans.
suggested_pairings: Enoki mushrooms stir-fried with bean sprouts

ingredients.name: Yardlong beans
ingredients.notes: Trim both ends and cut into 4–5 cm lengths.

ingredients.name: Straw mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim the bases, rinse quickly and drain; halve large mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Chili
ingredients.notes: Optional; omit for a mild dish.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount to balance the seasoning.

preparation_steps.instruction: Trim the ends and damaged sections of the beans, cut into bite-sized lengths, rinse and drain.
Clean the mushroom bases, rinse quickly and drain; halve any large mushrooms. Slice the scallions and chili, if using.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a pan and stir-fry the straw mushrooms for about a minute until they begin to soften.
Add the beans, raise the heat and keep tossing. Season with salt and sugar, and stir-fry for about 3–5 minutes until the beans are just tender.
Taste, add scallions, chili and pepper if desired, then turn off the heat.

dau-dua-xao-nam-rom-chay.media_alt_text: Vegetarian yardlong beans stir-fried with straw mushrooms until tender and lightly golden.

nam-kim-cham-xao-gia-do.name: Vegetarian Enoki Mushrooms with Bean Sprouts
nam-kim-cham-xao-gia-do.serving_basis: Two portions of enoki mushrooms and bean sprouts, quickly stir-fried for a vegetarian family meal.
nam-kim-cham-xao-gia-do.description: Enoki mushrooms and bean sprouts are quickly tossed with pickled mustard greens, leek and ginger; gentle sourness balances the crisp vegetables.
nam-kim-cham-xao-gia-do.finished_dish: The enoki are tender with a light bite, the sprouts stay crisp, and small amounts of pickled greens and bell pepper add color.
nam-kim-cham-xao-gia-do.serving: Serve immediately with steamed rice; do not leave the sprouts sitting in the hot pan.
tips: Rinse the mushrooms and sprouts separately, then drain them well.
Rinse the pickled greens if they taste too salty or sour, then squeeze dry.
Add the sprouts last and turn off the heat as soon as they soften slightly.
search_terms: vegetarian enoki mushrooms with bean sprouts
nam-kim-cham-xao-gia-do.image_alt: Vegetarian enoki mushroom and bean sprout stir-fry with pickled greens, ginger and bell pepper on a pale plate.
nam-kim-cham-xao-gia-do.time_note: About 15 minutes; the bean sprouts are added last and cooked quickly so they do not become watery.
suggested_pairings: Yardlong beans stir-fried with straw mushrooms

ingredients.name: Enoki mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim the roots, separate into small clusters and rinse.

ingredients.name: Pickled mustard greens
ingredients.notes: Use the stems, rinse to reduce salt and sourness, and slice.

ingredients.name: Bell pepper
ingredients.notes: Use red or green and dice.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into thin matchsticks.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Check the label to ensure it is plant-based.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the acidity of the pickles.

preparation_steps.instruction: Trim the roots from the enoki, separate into small clusters, rinse and drain. Rinse the bean sprouts and drain.
Rinse the pickled greens to reduce saltiness, if needed, and slice. Mince the leek, cut ginger into matchsticks and dice the bell pepper.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil and saute the leek until fragrant. Add the pickled greens and season with vegetarian oyster sauce, vegetarian seasoning and sugar.
Add the enoki and stir until they just soften and cook through.
Add the bean sprouts and toss quickly. Turn off the heat when they begin to soften, then mix in the ginger and bell pepper and serve.

nam-kim-cham-xao-gia-do.media_alt_text: Vegetarian enoki mushrooms stir-fried with bean sprouts, pickled greens, ginger and bell pepper.
